about.title: San Bruno Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Bruno households rely on countless everyday items — kitchen appliances, tools, vehicle parts, children's products — that are supposed to work as intended. When one doesn't, the results can be serious, whether the failure happens at home near El Camino Real or in a garage off Skyline Boulevard. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product had a defect in its design, manufacturing, or warning label, and that the defect caused harm. That standard can apply to the maker, the distributor, and even the retailer who sold it. If a product hurt you or someone in your family, keeping the item exactly as it was at the time of injury matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect San Bruno residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, free of charge and without any pressure to sign anything.

whyChoose.title: Why San Bruno Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease Your Burden
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was flawed and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the store that sold the product can potentially be held liable, giving an attorney more avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: An independent attorney can advise you early on how to properly keep and document the defective item, which is often central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Do I need to prove the company knew the product was dangerous?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you generally only need to show the product had a defect and that it caused your injury, not that the company knew or intended harm. An attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including packaging, instructions, or parts. Avoid repairs or alterations, since the product itself is often key evidence. An attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on safe storage and documentation.
